requirement: Number pads according to the datasheet electrical terminal mapping and the corresponding symbol: Physically separated copper lands may share a pad number when they represent the same electrical terminal. Use unnumbered pads only for non-electrical mechanical metal features that are intended to be soldered. A footprint shall not assign a net merely because a support, locator, shell, fastener, or other inserted feature is metal. Any intentional electrical bond must be numbered, represented in the symbol, and connected visibly through the schematic.

requirement: Use one pad for each terminal represented in the symbol. One terminal stays centered at its screw location. For two terminals that overlap in elevation, put their pads at equal distances to the left and right of the shared projected screw center. For three or more, put all pad centers on one circle centered there, equally spaced by 360 degrees divided by the terminal count: three at 120 degrees, four at 90 degrees, five at 72 degrees, and so on. Do not leave an extra electrical pad at the center of a fanned-out group.

Follow documented terminal order where available and label terminal tiers when needed to distinguish their physical locations.
